proofs.proof_tex:
Define the scalar identified set
\[
 \Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
 =\{\tau(\widetilde P):
       \widetilde P\in
       \mathcal M(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\}.
 \tag{33}
\]
Here \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}=\mathcal L(X,A,Y)\) is a law on the finite set \(\mathcal X\times\{0,1\}^2\), \(\widetilde P\) is a law on \(\mathcal X\times\{0,1\}^4\), and \(\tau(\widetilde P)=\widetilde E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\}\).  We use the declared support and overlap conditions \(\lambda_x>0\), \(0<p_x<1\), and \(0<r_{a,x}<1\), and finite budgets \(1\leq\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1<\infty\).  These conditions justify every conditioning operation below and ensure that every odds tilt and denominator is finite and positive.  No matrix inversion or rank condition is used.

Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\) and first let \(\widetilde P\in\mathcal M^{\circ}\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}observed\text{-}margin}\) identifies \(\lambda_x\), \(p_x\), and \(r_{a,x}\) with the corresponding full-law marginals and conditionals.  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\) then gives
\[
 r_{a,x}=\widetilde P\{Y(a)=1\mid A=a,X=x\}.
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}latent\text{-}ignorability}\) then removes \(A\) from the conditional potential-outcome risk.  With the definition of \(w_{a,x}\), this yields
\[
 r_{a,x}=(1-w_{a,x})\mu_{a,0,x}+w_{a,x}\mu_{a,1,x}.
 \tag{34}
\]
Bayes' rule is legal because all full-data cells are positive, and gives
\[
 \pi_x=\widetilde P(U=1\mid X=x)
      =p_xw_{1,x}+(1-p_x)w_{0,x}.
 \tag{35}
\]
The four positive \((A,U,X=x)\)-cell probabilities also give
\[
 \frac{\zeta_{1,1,x}\zeta_{0,0,x}}
      {\zeta_{1,0,x}\zeta_{0,1,x}}
 =\frac{w_{1,x}(1-w_{0,x})}
       {w_{0,x}(1-w_{1,x})}.
 \tag{36}
\]
After cancellation of the positive factor \(\lambda_x^2p_x(1-p_x)\), Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}treatment\text{-}odds\text{-}upper}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}treatment\text{-}odds\text{-}lower}\) are therefore exactly the condition \((w_{0,x},w_{1,x})\in D_{A,x}\).

On the strictly positive chart, let
\(\theta_{a,x}=\operatorname{OR}(\mu_{a,1,x},\mu_{a,0,x})\).  In each outcome cross product, the positive \((U,X=x)\)-margins cancel.  Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}outcome\text{-}odds\text{-}upper}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}outcome\text{-}odds\text{-}lower}\) thus imply
\[
 \Gamma_a^{-1}\leq\theta_{a,x}\leq\Gamma_a.
 \tag{37}
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\), applied to (34), uniquely identifies
\[
 \mu_{a,0,x}=\kappa(r_{a,x},w_{a,x},\theta_{a,x}),
 \;
 \mu_{a,1,x}
 =\frac{\theta_{a,x}\mu_{a,0,x}}
        {1+(\theta_{a,x}-1)\mu_{a,0,x}}.
 \tag{38}
\]
All quantities in (38) lie strictly between zero and one.  Subtracting (34) from the marginal potential-outcome mean and using (35) gives the exact bias decomposition
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widetilde E\{Y(a)\mid X=x\}
 &=(1-\pi_x)\mu_{a,0,x}+\pi_x\mu_{a,1,x}\\
 &=r_{a,x}+(\pi_x-w_{a,x})
      (\mu_{a,1,x}-\mu_{a,0,x})\\
 &=q_{a,x}(w_{0,x},w_{1,x};\theta_{a,x}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{39}
\]
This is a direct algebraic identity, not a definition of the causal mean.

Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\) optimizes (39) over (37), separately for the two outcome arms but at the same posterior pair.  Hence
\[
 H_x^-(w_{0,x},w_{1,x})
 \leq \widetilde E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x\}
 \leq H_x^+(w_{0,x},w_{1,x}).
 \tag{40}
\]
Minimizing and maximizing over the common feasible pair gives
\[
 \ell_x\leq
 \widetilde E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x\}
 \leq\upsilon_x.
 \tag{41}
\]
Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}one\text{-}arc\text{-}endpoint\text{-}reduction}\) strengthens this computable characterization: outside the two point-identified cases, both extrema in (41) are obtained on the single canonical arc
\[
 (w_{0,x},w_{1,x})=(W_{\Gamma_A}(t),t),\; 0<t<1,
 \tag{42}
\]
and the forward-arc candidates are exactly its images under relabeling \(U\).  If \(\Gamma_A=1\) or \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\), it instead gives
\(\ell_x=\upsilon_x=r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}\).

Multiplying (41) by \(\lambda_x>0\), summing over the finite support, and using \(\sum_x\lambda_x=1\) proves
\[
 L\leq\tau(\widetilde P)\leq R,
 \; \widetilde P\in\mathcal M^{\circ}.
 \tag{43}
\]
If \(\widetilde P\in\mathcal M\), Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}common\text{-}u\text{-}class}\) supplies a sequence \(\widetilde P_k\in\mathcal M^{\circ}\) converging to \(\widetilde P\) in the finite simplex.  The functional \(\tau\) is linear, hence continuous, so (43) passes to the limit.  This proves the outer bound
\[
 \Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq[L,R].
 \tag{44}
\]

We next construct compatible laws and thereby prove sharpness.  In every stratum choose an interior posterior pair \(d_x=(w_{0,x},w_{1,x})\in D_{A,x}\cap(0,1)^2\) and tilts \(\theta_{a,x}\in[\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a]\).  Define
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
 \widetilde P(A=1,U=1\mid X=x)=p_xw_{1,x},
 &\widetilde P(A=1,U=0\mid X=x)=p_x(1-w_{1,x}),\\
 \widetilde P(A=0,U=1\mid X=x)=(1-p_x)w_{0,x},
 &\widetilde P(A=0,U=0\mid X=x)=(1-p_x)(1-w_{0,x}).
\end{array}
\tag{45}
\]
Observed overlap and interiority of \(d_x\) make all four entries positive.  Define \(\mu_{a,0,x}\) and \(\mu_{a,1,x}\) by (38).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) puts them in \((0,1)\) and makes (34) hold exactly.  Conditional on \((X=x,U=u)\), draw \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) independently as Bernoulli variables with success probabilities \(\mu_{0,u,x}\) and \(\mu_{1,u,x}\), use the same conditional law at both treatment values, and set
\[
 Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0).
 \tag{46}
\]
The conditional construction proves \((Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid(X,U)\); it does not assume this relation after the fact.  Equations (34), (45), and (46) reproduce the observed conditional law of \((A,Y)\) in stratum \(x\).  Equation (36), membership in \(D_{A,x}\), and (37) verify the four odds inequalities.  Assigning \(\widetilde P(X=x)=\lambda_x\) therefore gives a law in \(\mathcal M^{\circ}\), and (39) gives its causal arm means.

The parameter set
\[
 \mathcal D_x^{\circ}
 =\{D_{A,x}\cap(0,1)^2\}
   \times[\Gamma_0^{-1},\Gamma_0]
   \times[\Gamma_1^{-1},\Gamma_1]
 \tag{47}
\]
is connected.  Indeed, the coordinatewise logit map sends its posterior-pair factor to the convex strip
\[
 \{(s_0,s_1)\in\mathbb R^2:
      |s_1-s_0|\leq\log\Gamma_A\}.
 \tag{48}
\]
The remaining two factors are intervals.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\) and Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) make the contrast map continuous on (47).

The one-arc theorem also shows that the minimum and maximum \(\ell_x,\upsilon_x\) are attained inside (47): in the non-point-identified case its optimizer satisfies \(0<t<1\) in (42), while in either point-identified case one may take \(w_0=w_1=1/2\) and \(\theta_{0,x}=\theta_{1,x}=1\).  A continuous image of a connected set is an interval.  Its image lies in \([\ell_x,\upsilon_x]\) by (40) and contains both endpoints, hence it equals that interval.  The finite product \(\prod_x\mathcal D_x^{\circ}\) is connected, and the continuous weighted-sum map has image
\[
 \left[\sum_x\lambda_x\ell_x,
       \sum_x\lambda_x\upsilon_x\right]=[L,R].
 \tag{49}
\]
Applying the construction (45)--(46) to every point in this product proves the stronger fact
\[
 [L,R]\subseteq\{\tau(\widetilde P):\widetilde P\in\mathcal M^{\circ}\}
 \subseteq\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
 \tag{50}
\]
Together, (44) and (50) establish \(\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})=[L,R]\), and in particular imply the stated infimum, supremum, and closure conclusions for \(\mathcal M^{\circ}\).

For completeness, the boundary assertions follow without assigning an odds ratio at a null cell.  For finite \(\Gamma_A\), substitution in the two exposure inequalities shows that a feasible pair with a zero coordinate is \((0,0)\), and one with a unit coordinate is \((1,1)\).  Approximate these pairs by \((\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\) and \((1-\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon)\).  They remain in \(D_{A,x}\cap(0,1)^2\), and Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\) gives convergence of all adjusted means.  The corresponding laws from (45)--(46) converge in the finite simplex, so their limits belong to \(\mathcal M\) and attain the corner contrast.  At an interior posterior pair, any coupling of the two Bernoulli marginals may replace conditional independence.  If that coupling has zero cells, mix it with an arbitrarily small amount of the independent coupling; this preserves both Bernoulli marginals, makes every joint outcome cell positive, preserves conditional independence from \(A\), and converges back to the selected coupling.  Thus every such coupling defines a law in the closed class.

All identifying equalities above came from the maintained assumptions and the explicit construction.  Rosenbaum--Rubin is used only as a historical comparator for fixed binary-confounder sensitivity tuples; no equality or inclusion involving its Sections 2--4 class is used or proved.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\) and finite budgets \(1\leq\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1<\infty\).  When \(\Gamma_A>1\), define
\[
 W_{\Gamma_A}(t)=\frac{\Gamma_A t}{1+(\Gamma_A-1)t},\; 0\leq t\leq1.
\]
For \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and \(1<\Gamma_a<\infty\), let
\[
 z_{a,\Gamma_a}(w)=\kappa(r_{a,x},w,\Gamma_a),\;
 \Delta_{a,\Gamma_a}(w)=
 \frac{\Gamma_a z_{a,\Gamma_a}(w)}
      {1+(\Gamma_a-1)z_{a,\Gamma_a}(w)}-z_{a,\Gamma_a}(w),
\]
and set \(\Delta_{a,1}(w)=0\).  For \(0<w<1\) and \(\Gamma_a>1\),
\[
 -\frac{\Delta_{a,\Gamma_a}(w)}{w}
 <\frac{d}{dw}\Delta_{a,\Gamma_a}(w)
 <\frac{\Delta_{a,\Gamma_a}(w)}{1-w}.
\]
If \(\Gamma_A>1\) and \((\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\neq(1,1)\), then on \(0<w_1<w_0<1\), with \(e=w_0-w_1\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
H_x^+(w_0,w_1)
 &=r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}
 +e\{(1-p_x)\Delta_{1,\Gamma_1}(w_1)
       +p_x\Delta_{0,\Gamma_0}(w_0)\},\\
H_x^-(w_0,w_1)
 &=r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}
 -e\{(1-p_x)\Delta_{1,\Gamma_1}(1-w_1)
       +p_x\Delta_{0,\Gamma_0}(1-w_0)\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently \(H_x^+\) is strictly increasing in \(w_0\) and strictly decreasing in \(w_1\), whereas \(H_x^-\) is strictly decreasing in \(w_0\) and strictly increasing in \(w_1\).  Neither relevant extremum over \(D_{A,x}\) has a two-dimensional interior optimizer, every non-point-identified optimizer saturates a treatment-odds inequality, complementing \(U\) maps every forward-arc optimizer to a reverse-arc optimizer with the same objective value, and
\[
 \ell_x=\min_{0\leq t\leq1}H_x^-(W_{\Gamma_A}(t),t),
 \;
 \upsilon_x=\max_{0\leq t\leq1}H_x^+(W_{\Gamma_A}(t),t).
\]
If \(\Gamma_A=1\) or \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\), then instead
\(\ell_x=\upsilon_x=r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix the stratum and suppress its index.  The proof uses implicit differentiation, strict coordinate monotonicity, and the involution that relabels the two states of \(U\).

First take \(r\in(0,1)\), \(\vartheta>1\), and \(0<w<1\).  Put
\[
 f(z)=\frac{\vartheta z}{1+(\vartheta-1)z},
 \; z(w)=\kappa(r,w,\vartheta),
 \; \Delta(w)=f\{z(w)\}-z(w).
 \tag{16}
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) gives \(0<z(w)<f\{z(w)\}<1\) and
\[
 r=(1-w)z(w)+wf\{z(w)\}=z(w)+w\Delta(w).
 \tag{17}
\]
Because
\[
 f'(z)=\frac{\vartheta}{\{1+(\vartheta-1)z\}^2}>0,
 \;
 D(w)=1-w+wf'\{z(w)\}>0,
 \tag{18}
\]
the derivative of the left side of the mixture equation with respect to \(z\) is nonzero.  Implicit differentiation is therefore legal and yields
\[
 z'(w)=-\frac{\Delta(w)}{D(w)},
 \;
 \Delta'(w)=\{f'\{z(w)\}-1\}z'(w).
 \tag{19}
\]
Combining (18)--(19), equation by equation, gives
\[
 \Delta(w)+w\Delta'(w)=\frac{\Delta(w)}{D(w)}>0,
 \;
 \Delta(w)-(1-w)\Delta'(w)
 =\frac{\Delta(w)f'\{z(w)\}}{D(w)}>0.
 \tag{20}
\]
Division in (20) is valid because \(0<w<1\), and it proves
\[
 -\frac{\Delta(w)}{w}<\Delta'(w)
 <\frac{\Delta(w)}{1-w}.
 \tag{21}
\]
This proves the asserted derivative inequalities for every nontrivial arm budget.  The convention \(\Delta_{a,1}=0\) covers a trivial arm without applying the strict inequalities to it.

We next record the relabeling identity.  For a posterior pair \(d=(w_0,w_1)\), define
\[
 d^c=(1-w_0,1-w_1),\quad \pi^c=1-\pi.
 \tag{22}
\]
If \((m_0,m_1)\) is the unique feasible risk pair at mixture weight \(w_a\) and odds ratio \(\vartheta\), then \((m_1,m_0)\) is feasible at weight \(1-w_a\) and odds ratio \(\vartheta^{-1}\).  Indeed,
\[
 w_am_1+(1-w_a)m_0=r_{a,x},
 \;
 \operatorname{OR}(m_0,m_1)=\vartheta^{-1}.
 \tag{23}
\]
Uniqueness in Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) therefore identifies this as the pair used by the adjusted-arm map.  Since
\[
 \pi^c-(1-w_a)=-(\pi-w_a),
 \; m_0-m_1=-(m_1-m_0),
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}adjusted\text{-}arm\text{-}mean}\) gives
\[
 q_{a,x}(d^c;\vartheta^{-1})=q_{a,x}(d;\vartheta).
 \tag{24}
\]
The endpoint set \(\{\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a\}\) is invariant under reciprocation.  Hence
\[
 q_{a,x}^{\pm}(d^c)=q_{a,x}^{\pm}(d),
 \; H_x^{\pm}(d^c)=H_x^{\pm}(d).
 \tag{25}
\]
The two cross-product inequalities defining \(D_{A,x}\) are also exchanged by \(d\mapsto d^c\), so this involution preserves the exposure region and maps its forward half to its reverse half.

Now suppose \(0<w_1<w_0<1\) and put \(e=w_0-w_1\).  The definition of \(\pi\) gives
\[
 \pi-w_1=(1-p_x)e>0,
 \; \pi-w_0=-p_xe<0,
 \tag{26}
\]
where strictness uses the observed overlap condition \(0<p_x<1\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\), followed by (24) for the reciprocal tilt, gives
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
q^+_{1,x}=r_{1,x}+(1-p_x)e\Delta_{1,\Gamma_1}(w_1),
&q^-_{1,x}=r_{1,x}-(1-p_x)e\Delta_{1,\Gamma_1}(1-w_1),\\
q^-_{0,x}=r_{0,x}-p_xe\Delta_{0,\Gamma_0}(w_0),
&q^+_{0,x}=r_{0,x}+p_xe\Delta_{0,\Gamma_0}(1-w_0).
\end{array}
\tag{27}
\]
Subtracting the appropriate two entries proves the two displayed formulas in the statement.

Write
\[
 B=(1-p_x)\Delta_{1,\Gamma_1}(w_1)
   +p_x\Delta_{0,\Gamma_0}(w_0).
\]
At least one summand is strictly positive because \((\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\neq(1,1)\).  Since \(e<w_0\), the lower inequality in (21) gives
\[
 \frac{\partial H_x^+}{\partial w_0}
 =B+ep_x\Delta'_{0,\Gamma_0}(w_0)
 >(1-p_x)\Delta_{1,\Gamma_1}(w_1)
   +p_x\Delta_{0,\Gamma_0}(w_0)\left(1-\frac e{w_0}\right)>0.
 \tag{28}
\]
Terms belonging to an arm with \(\Gamma_a=1\) are simply zero.  Since \(e<1-w_1\), the upper inequality in (21) similarly gives
\[
 \frac{\partial H_x^+}{\partial w_1}
 =-B+e(1-p_x)\Delta'_{1,\Gamma_1}(w_1)
 <-p_x\Delta_{0,\Gamma_0}(w_0)
  -(1-p_x)\Delta_{1,\Gamma_1}(w_1)
       \left(1-\frac e{1-w_1}\right)<0.
 \tag{29}
\]

For the lower objective put
\[
 C=(1-p_x)\Delta_{1,\Gamma_1}(1-w_1)
   +p_x\Delta_{0,\Gamma_0}(1-w_0).
\]
Using respectively \(e<w_0\), the upper inequality in (21) at \(1-w_0\), \(e<1-w_1\), and the lower inequality in (21) at \(1-w_1\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \frac{\partial H_x^-}{\partial w_0}
 &=-C+ep_x\Delta'_{0,\Gamma_0}(1-w_0)\\
 &<-(1-p_x)\Delta_{1,\Gamma_1}(1-w_1)
   -p_x\Delta_{0,\Gamma_0}(1-w_0)\left(1-\frac e{w_0}\right)<0,\\
 \frac{\partial H_x^-}{\partial w_1}
 &=C+e(1-p_x)\Delta'_{1,\Gamma_1}(1-w_1)\\
 &>p_x\Delta_{0,\Gamma_0}(1-w_0)
   +(1-p_x)\Delta_{1,\Gamma_1}(1-w_1)
       \left(1-\frac e{1-w_1}\right)>0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{30}
\]
Thus no relevant optimizer lies in the two-dimensional interior of either half of \(D_{A,x}\).

For an interior reverse-half point, the exposure inequalities are equivalent to
\[
 w_1\leq w_0\leq W_{\Gamma_A}(w_1).
 \tag{31}
\]
If the upper inequality is strict, increasing \(w_0\) to \(W_{\Gamma_A}(w_1)\) remains feasible; by (28) it strictly raises \(H_x^+\), and by (30) it strictly lowers \(H_x^-\).  Hence the upper maximizer and lower minimizer in the reverse half lie on
\[
 (w_0,w_1)=(W_{\Gamma_A}(t),t),\; 0<t<1.
 \tag{32}
\]
Equation (25) carries every forward-half candidate to the reverse half without changing either objective.  On the diagonal and at the constant-confounder corners, \(\pi=w_0=w_1\), so \(H_x^-=H_x^+=r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}\).  For every \(0<t<1\), however, \(W_{\Gamma_A}(t)>t\), and (27) makes \(H_x^+\) strictly larger and \(H_x^-\) strictly smaller than this diagonal value.  Therefore no diagonal point or constant-\(U\) corner is optimal in the non-point-identified case.  Continuity at \(t=0,1\), supplied by Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\), now proves the two one-dimensional endpoint formulas and shows that their optimizers actually have \(0<t<1\).

Finally, if \(\Gamma_A=1\), the two exposure inequalities imply \(w_0=w_1\), whence \(\pi=w_a\) and every adjusted arm mean equals \(r_{a,x}\).  If \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\), both outcome tilts equal one, so the two latent risks in each arm are equal and again every adjusted arm mean equals its observed arm risk.  In either case \(\ell_x=\upsilon_x=r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}\), as claimed.
added_lemmas.justification: Strict tilt-gap derivatives collapse each non-point-identified two-dimensional exposure optimization to one canonical odds-boundary arc.
added_lemmas.gap: The fixed-tuple binary-confounder comparator does not supply this common-posterior endpoint reduction, and no historical class transfer is asserted.
added_lemmas.consumer: The sharp envelope, fixed-input certificate, parametric tipping atlas, and strict-gap witness can enumerate one exposure arc and recover the other by relabeling \(U\).

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: For fixed rational observed summaries and rational finite budgets, \(\mathsf{CERT}\) first treats \(\Gamma_A=1\) and \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\) as the point-identified cases.  Otherwise it sets \(W_{\Gamma_A}(t)=\Gamma_A t/\{1+(\Gamma_A-1)t\}\) and evaluates only the canonical reverse-arc objectives \(H_x^-(W_{\Gamma_A}(t),t)\) and \(H_x^+(W_{\Gamma_A}(t),t)\) for \(t\in[0,1]\); the forward arc is represented by complementing \(U\) and is not enumerated separately.  The procedure treats each \(\Gamma_a=1\) branch separately, adjoins the legal quadratic-root variables for nontrivial arms, evaluates \(t=0,1\) as the constant-\(U\) corners, saturates every stationary ideal by all cleared denominators, legal-root derivatives, and branch-boundary polynomials, isolates generic zero-dimensional stationary candidates by iterated resultants and Sturm sequences, and validates every isolated candidate against the original equations and inequalities by rational interval Newton tests.  An identically vanishing resultant, a legal-root collision, or a positive-dimensional stationary continuum is passed to cylindrical algebraic decomposition rather than discarded.  For the fixed input, \(\mathsf{CERT}\) returns real-algebraic endpoint values, rational isolating intervals, and exact membership certificates; it does not return a symbolic atlas over varying inputs.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The proved complement invariance and strict coordinate monotonicities make the forward arc and every two-dimensional interior candidate redundant; the certificate must use the canonical one-dimensional arc while retaining all exceptional and degeneracy cases.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: For rational or real-algebraic observed summaries and endpoints of \(\mathcal B\), \(\mathsf{ATLAS}\) treats \((\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\in\mathcal B\) as parameters.  It separates the point-identified strata \(\Gamma_A=1\) and \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\); on every remaining stratum it sets \(W_{\Gamma_A}(t)=\Gamma_A t/\{1+(\Gamma_A-1)t\}\), represents the forward exposure arc by the complement involution on \(U\), and constructs the lower and upper objectives only on the canonical arc \((w_0,w_1)=(W_{\Gamma_A}(t),t)\).  It then eliminates the legal mixture-root and one-dimensional stationary variables, including all saturated denominator and endpoint cases, and performs parametric cylindrical algebraic decomposition over \(K_{\mathrm{in}}\).  The output consists of exact quantifier-free sign cells and algebraic optimizer strata, including legal-root collisions and stationary continua; rational isolating intervals are returned only after a zero-dimensional specialization.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The parametric elimination variables should reflect the proved one-arc endpoint representation and explicitly stratify the point-identified and singular cases.

proposed.statement: The ATE identified set over the closed class \(\mathcal M(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\) is exactly \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{com}}=[L,R]\), with \(L\) and \(R\) defined by one common \((w_{0,x},w_{1,x})\in D_{A,x}\) per stratum.  Every endpoint is attained by a law in \(\mathcal M\): at an interior selected pair the law uses the selected feasible risks as conditional Bernoulli marginals and any coupling of \((Y(0),Y(1))\) given \((X,U)\), while a constant-\(U\) boundary pair is attained as the finite-simplex limit of such strictly positive laws.  Over \(\mathcal M^{\circ}\), \(\inf\tau=L\), \(\sup\tau=R\), and the closure of the identified set is \([L,R]\); endpoint attainment is asserted there only when an attaining law is itself strictly positive.  The result is a theorem about the maintained common-binary-confounder class and does not assert that this bounded class, its arbitrary conditional potential-outcome coupling, or its finite-simplex closure is the class defined in Rosenbaum--Rubin Sections 2--4.
proposed.justification: This is the sharp population kernel: both potential-outcome arms are simultaneously realized through one latent confounder, and the nontrivial endpoints reduce to one canonical exposure-odds arc.
proposed.gap: Rosenbaum--Rubin evaluate fixed binary-confounder sensitivity tuples; Ciocănea-Teodorescu--Gabriel--Sjölander use distinct exposure-standardization parameters; and Dorn--Guo prove sharpness for a different propensity-only model.  None gives this closed bounded common-binary-\(U\) iff envelope or its one-arc reduction.
proposed.consumer: Investigators obtain the narrowest logically valid ATE interval under the maintained common-binary-confounder budgets and a one-dimensional endpoint map suitable for exact certification.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The target now directly depends on the canonical one-arc reduction used in its strengthened attainment argument; the formal claim itself is unchanged.

proposed.name: Degeneracy-aware one-arc semialgebraic certificate
proposed.construction: For fixed rational observed summaries and rational finite budgets, \(\mathsf{CERT}\) first treats \(\Gamma_A=1\) and \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\) as the point-identified cases.  Otherwise it sets \(W_{\Gamma_A}(t)=\Gamma_A t/\{1+(\Gamma_A-1)t\}\) and evaluates only the canonical reverse-arc objectives \(H_x^-(W_{\Gamma_A}(t),t)\) and \(H_x^+(W_{\Gamma_A}(t),t)\) for \(t\in[0,1]\); the forward arc is represented by complementing \(U\) and is not enumerated separately.  The procedure treats each \(\Gamma_a=1\) branch separately, adjoins the legal quadratic-root variables for nontrivial arms, evaluates \(t=0,1\) as the constant-\(U\) corners, saturates every stationary ideal by all cleared denominators, legal-root derivatives, and branch-boundary polynomials, isolates generic zero-dimensional stationary candidates by iterated resultants and Sturm sequences, and validates every isolated candidate against the original equations and inequalities by rational interval Newton tests.  An identically vanishing resultant, a legal-root collision, or a positive-dimensional stationary continuum is passed to cylindrical algebraic decomposition rather than discarded.  For the fixed input, \(\mathsf{CERT}\) returns real-algebraic endpoint values, rational isolating intervals, and exact membership certificates; it does not return a symbolic atlas over varying inputs.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The construction and its symbol/input metadata must jointly reflect the canonical one-dimensional exposure arc and the explicit point-identified strata.

proposed.name: Canonical-arc parametric cylindrical-algebraic atlas procedure
proposed.construction: For rational or real-algebraic observed summaries and endpoints of \(\mathcal B\), \(\mathsf{ATLAS}\) treats \((\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\in\mathcal B\) as parameters.  It separates the point-identified strata \(\Gamma_A=1\) and \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\); on every remaining stratum it sets \(W_{\Gamma_A}(t)=\Gamma_A t/\{1+(\Gamma_A-1)t\}\), represents the forward exposure arc by the complement involution on \(U\), and constructs the lower and upper objectives only on the canonical arc \((w_0,w_1)=(W_{\Gamma_A}(t),t)\).  It then eliminates the legal mixture-root and one-dimensional stationary variables, including all saturated denominator and endpoint cases, and performs parametric cylindrical algebraic decomposition over \(K_{\mathrm{in}}\).  The output consists of exact quantifier-free sign cells and algebraic optimizer strata, including legal-root collisions and stationary continua; rational isolating intervals are returned only after a zero-dimensional specialization.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The atlas construction and metadata must eliminate only the canonical-arc stationary variables while preserving explicit exceptional and singular strata.

prose_updates.tldr: For binary treatment, outcome, and one shared latent binary confounder within finitely many observed strata, the exact ATE interval over the closed finite-simplex sensitivity class is obtained by optimizing both potential-outcome arms over the same posterior pair.  A strict tilt-gap derivative argument reduces every non-point-identified stratum endpoint to the single canonical arc \(w_0=W_{\Gamma_A}(t),w_1=t\); complementing \(U\) recovers the forward arc.  The fixed-input certificate and parametric tipping atlas therefore operate one-dimensionally while retaining point-identified cases, null-cell limits, denominator checks, root collisions, and stationary continua.  The complete rational transcript \((\mathrm{C1})\)--\((\mathrm{C10})\) certifies a stable strict gap relative to the internal separate-pair relaxation.  Regular zero-frontier points have the proved root-\(n\) normal-displacement law, while uniformly honest inference at ties, collisions, continua, and higher-order contact remains the singular-only open question.

project_justification.gap: The fixed-tuple binary-confounder calculation of Rosenbaum and Rubin does not optimize this maintained bounded common-posterior region or identify its finite-simplex closure.  Propensity-only, arbitrary-confounder, and exposure-standardization models use different primitives and do not provide the common-\(U\) one-arc envelope, its exact certificate, or its multibudget tipping geometry.
project_justification.niche: The restriction is scientifically interpretable and algebraically low dimensional: strict coordinate monotonicity reduces the shared-posterior optimization to one exposure-odds arc without discarding the compatibility information that separates it from armwise relaxation.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the iff ATE interval, endpoint-attaining laws, a canonical one-arc reduction, a degeneracy-complete fixed-input certificate, a parametric algebraic tipping atlas, the complete \((\mathrm{C1})\)--\((\mathrm{C10})\) strict-gap witness, point-identification and Manski-limit reductions, and pointwise regular-frontier inference; only singular uniform frontier inference remains open.

sampling_model.design: Observational sampling from a fixed population law; population partial identification is primary and frontier inference is secondary.
sampling_model.units: Independent draws \((X_i,A_i,Y_i)\sim P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) with finite \(\mathcal X\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment may depend on \((X,U)\); every candidate full-data law restores conditional ignorability given the same binary \(U\) for both potential outcomes.
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed stratum satisfies \(0<p_x<1\); the closed population class retains constant-\(U\) limits, and latent treatment positivity vanishes only along the joint all-budget path used for Manski recovery.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The finite-cell summaries \((\lambda_x,p_x,r_{0,x},r_{1,x})\) are estimated by empirical frequencies.  At a unique nondegenerate active branch with nonzero budget gradient, the regular inference theorem gives the explicit root-\(n\) normal displacement and standard-error constant; uniform inference is open only at optimizer ties, legal-root collisions, stationary continua, and higher-order algebraic contact.

prose_updates.related_work: Rosenbaum and Rubin \cite{RosenbaumRubin1983Sensitivity} are retained only as the fixed-tuple binary-confounder comparator; the verified source does not establish equality with, or an inclusion direction for, this paper's arm-specific two-sided bounded class, arbitrary conditional potential-outcome coupling, or finite-simplex closure.  VanderWeele and Arah \cite{VanderWeeleArah2011Bias} motivate the binary-confounder bias decomposition.  Ding and VanderWeele \cite{DingVanderWeele2016WithoutAssumptions} give a sharp arbitrary-\(U\) relative-risk factor, while Tan \cite{Tan2006MarginalSensitivity}, Yadlowsky et al. \cite{YadlowskyEtAl2022Bounds}, and Dorn and Guo \cite{DornGuo2023QuantileBalancing} study propensity-based marginal sensitivity models.  Ciocănea-Teodorescu, Gabriel, and Sjölander \cite{CiocaneaGabrielSjolander2022Marginal} use exposure-standardization sensitivity parameters, and Nabi et al. \cite{NabiEtAl2024SemiparametricSensitivity} provide an adjacent tilt-model framework.  These models are generally non-nested with the maintained common-binary-\(U\) class, so no numerical dominance is claimed.  The separate-posterior-pair interval is instead an internal relaxation obtained by dropping only the shared-pair constraint, and the complete rational transcript proves a strict open-set gap against it.  Masten and Poirier \cite{MastenPoirier2020BreakdownFrontier} motivate the tipping frontier, Fang and Santos \cite{FangSantos2019InferenceDirectional} motivate nonsmooth inference, and Manski \cite{Manski1990TreatmentResponse} is recovered only in the joint infinite-budget limit with vanishing latent positivity.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The one-arc theorem removes two-dimensional interior searches and duplicate forward-arc enumeration.  The worked rational witness is fully certified by the explicit \((\mathrm{C1})\)--\((\mathrm{C10})\) polynomial, Sturm, interval-Newton, legal-cell, and competitor transcript.  The fixed-input certificate and parametric atlas remain exact mathematical procedures rather than complexity guarantees for a software implementation.  The regular inference theorem is pointwise and applies only to a unique nondegenerate active branch with nonzero budget gradient; uniformly honest Hausdorff inference at ties, legal-root collisions, stationary continua, and contact order \(k\geq2\) remains open.  No historical class transfer or dominance comparison with a non-nested published sensitivity model is claimed.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The sharp population interval concerns the maintained single-binary-confounder class with finite categorical \(X\), interior observed cells, finite odds budgets, and its explicitly defined finite-simplex closure.  Nontrivial stratum endpoints lie on the canonical reverse exposure arc, with the forward arc recovered by complementing \(U\); \(\Gamma_A=1\) and \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\) remain point-identified exceptions.  The odds ratio is not assigned a value at null cells.  The \((\mathrm{C1})\)--\((\mathrm{C10})\) transcript establishes the displayed common-versus-separate witness and its open-neighborhood strictness.  The zero-tipping surface has a parametric algebraic atlas, and unique regular branches have pointwise root-\(n\) normal-displacement inference; the open question is restricted to uniform inference on singular frontier strata.  Manski recovery is only the joint all-budget limit along vanishing latent treatment positivity.  Rosenbaum--Rubin remains a fixed-tuple comparator, not an asserted owner or exact supermodel or submodel of the maintained class.

statement_notes.justification: This is the sharp population kernel: both potential-outcome arms are jointly realizable through the same latent confounder, and strict tilt-gap monotonicity makes the endpoint map one-dimensional.
statement_notes.gap: The fixed-tuple Rosenbaum--Rubin comparator, exposure-standardization procedures, and propensity-only marginal sensitivity bounds do not give this closed bounded common-binary-\(U\) iff envelope or its canonical-arc reduction.
statement_notes.consumer: Investigators receive the narrowest valid ATE interval under the declared common-confounder budgets together with a one-dimensional map that exact certification and tipping analysis can consume.
